key_insight: Neural networks can end up with similar outputs after common training while still carrying measurable differences in their internal representations from earlier training history.
engineering_relevance: For AI-enabled constitutive modeling and other engineering workflows, matching accuracy alone may hide persistent model-state differences that affect interpretability, transfer, and reproducibility.
method: Paired CNNs started from identical weights and were trained in reversed task orders before a shared deterministic relaxation phase.
Representation-history scores and prediction disagreement were measured after common training, with additional controls for longer relaxation, rotated MNIST, and activation function changes.
Fresh linear probes tested whether the hidden differences still mattered for class information access.
evidence_signal: Across 20 MNIST pairs, 16 met behavioral matching yet still showed a mean representation-history score of 0.139 and about 3.1% prediction disagreement; similar persistence remained after 50,000 updates.
watch_item: The effect is protocol-scoped and depends on the specific training setup, so it should not be assumed to generalize without checking task order, architecture, optimizer, and activation choices.
paper_title: Behavioral Convergence Without Representational Convergence: Persistent Training-History Dependence in Neural Networks
